scope: CMAZE-T arm columns ONLY. Every T7 (Shapes3D, K*=32) panel was built from staged artefacts; nothing is needed for those.
why: w16 maze-wm (scripts/w16_cmaze_t.py::full, branch w16/maze-wm 9f80f59) trains the frozen codec, frozen state encoder, CLU store, controls, blind arms and matched rivals IN-PROCESS and never writes any of them to disk. The primary record w16-maze-wm/t1/A1_test_seed{0,1,2}.json holds aggregate scores only, with no per-transition prediction. So these objects do NOT exist on the ThinkPad either (C:/chlu/outputs/w16-maze-wm/ holds the same JSONs). Re-training here would be a new TEST-leg run with a new codec, and the task forbids both.
what_would_unblock: A persistence-only re-run of the SCORED config on the ThinkPad: `python scripts/w16_cmaze_t.py full <seed> <out> --leg test --latent 128 --K 2 --atoms 6 --ridge 1.0 --iface none --tag A1`, patched to pickle the objects below. It must first reproduce A1_test_seed<N>.json's ROWS/ROLLOUT/DELETION numbers to every digit, or it is not the scored object. That is a Hub/ledger decision, because it re-executes the TEST leg. This spoke does not make it.

paths_needed.what: the frozen codec (latent 128), with a param hash written beside it
paths_needed.for: decoding every CLU/control read to s_t+1; the hash-asserted 'same codec'

paths_needed.what: the downdated CLU and the rivals retrained without colour 1
ALTERNATIVE to all of the above: per-transition emitted codes for every arm on the capped TEST split (seen/pair/nway/value) plus the deletion arms, keyed by split index
paths_needed.for: every arm column; lighter, needs no model load

seeds: seed 0 is enough for the figure. Seeds 1-2 are the same paths with seed1/seed2, and are needed only if the rule_a family row (seed 2) is to carry arm columns.
